notes:
- Fixed tag normalization so equipment ending in -A, -B, or -C remains a separate asset by default
- Existing site profiles using the previous untouched default are updated automatically, while custom and taught endings remain under site control
- Improved startup update checks so a cached response or slower connection does not hide a newly published version

- Electrical feed chains now persist as the hierarchy: within one building and one top-down discipline (Electrical, LSS, Security), the Easy Power / Cable Schedule chain nests intact across UPN boundaries — GIS at the top under 602 Medium Voltage, everything it feeds beneath it. Each equipment's register row keeps its own MEL building and UPN
- For that gear the feed sources outrank the MEL's System Parent column, so an administrative MEL entry cannot sever the chain (it stays recorded as a runner-up)
- Chains still break where they should: a feed crossing buildings or disciplines demotes to a dependency, exactly as before — the RIO rule is unchanged
- MEL panel-side spellings (-A/-B/-C) tie to the Easy Power spelling: one piece of equipment, MEL attributes attached

- Teach a tag ending by highlighting it: click any tag in the results drawer, select the ending (like "-C"), and one button removes it from every tag. Behind the click it becomes an ordinary normalize rule, saved to your site profile and editable in the Studio like any other rule
- A trailing -C now counts as a panel side out of the box, alongside -A, -B, -P, -S, and -OUTPUT
- Every shipped rule's name and description is rewritten in plain language — what it does, with an example, and when to change it — instead of implementation notes

- The Comparison tab no longer buries Easy Power results when a MEL is loaded. "No Comparison" now splits into two filters that mean opposite things: "Missing from Extracted" (working-copy rows this build did not produce — real findings) and "Not in Working Copy" (register rows the MEL seeds by construction — expected). The combined view orders discrepancies and gaps first, matches next, and the MEL-seeded extras last

- SSManagement 4.0: the compiler generation formally continues the SSManagement line. The original app (which ended at 3.5.0) is retired as SSManagement-Legacy; this app now owns the SSManagement name and release channel end to end
- The GitHub repositories are renamed to match: source noahfgarrett/SSManagement, releases noahfgarrett/SSManagement-Releases. Copies installed before this release keep updating — the old channel address redirects, and both channel names remain trusted
- Everything from the compiler generation is carried forward unchanged: MEL-first compilation, the partition fold, description-driven nesting with drag-to-teach, milestone ladders, EXTO exports, and the Legend Trainer

- The app is SSManagement again: title, header, guide, and download filenames all carry the name (documents in → ssm out stays). The update channel, saved profiles, and site rules are untouched — existing installs update normally and keep everything
- Hierarchy search no longer stalls while typing: broad queries that matched tens of thousands of rows went from about a second per keystroke to under 50ms, showing the first 400 match branches with a running total and a prompt to narrow
- The Site Profile Studio opens its tabs much faster: the Visual Trainer's full-model evaluation is paid once right after a build finishes (in the background) and reused across studio visits, and the Test & Publish impact summary is cached instead of re-evaluating the whole model on every repaint
- The built-in profile is renamed "SSManagement Default"

- Fixed the Legend Trainer's region-selection preview freezing at "Rendering page…": a wiring error in the anatomy binder crashed the interface refresh the moment the preview opened, before the page ever started drawing, and the busy state could never clear
- The preview now also survives any future rendering error by showing the failure instead of freezing on the loading frame

- Large-workbook imports and builds are ~35% faster end to end (measured on 260,000 rows: about 22s down to about 14s), with byte-identical output
- Workbooks parse in SheetJS dense mode and the sheet scan takes a row-array fast path, cutting import and tab-scanning time roughly in half
- Tag identity resolution (cleanTag, tagKey, register tags) now memoizes per input with rule-engine-generation invalidation, and the rule engine caches by caller input, precompiles suffix endings and exclude lists, and skips redundant re-cleaning in per-rule checks
- No behavior changes: the golden compatibility suite and new dense-vs-sparse identity tests prove identical output on every fixture

- The shipped built-in profile is now the universal SSM Compiler ruleset (renamed "SSM Compiler Default"): MEL seeding, modern source-priority resolution, and Rev21 EXTO columns are on out of the box, so a MEL-only build works no matter which profile is selected
- The compiler now keeps its own profile storage. It previously shared SSManagement's, so on a machine running both apps it silently loaded SSManagement's store — including a legacy-frozen active profile that produced an empty build
- Real-world MEL headers now detect: tag columns like "Equipment Tag Number" / "Tag No." are recognized when UPN or System Parent columns corroborate, and tabs named "Master Equipment List" or "MEL" are treated as MELs by name
- An empty build now names its actual blocker (unrecognized MEL header row, seeding disabled in the active profile, or a MEL-looking tab in the wrong selection group) instead of the blanket "no hierarchy rows" toast
- The frozen Eagle legacy behavior survives as an internal compatibility baseline for the regression suite; it is no longer offered in the picker

- A MEL alone now builds end to end from the UI: the build button enables with only a MEL selected, headers are found whether they start in row 1, 2, or 3, and the result opens straight into the SSM Hierarchy view (Electrical Flow only exists when Easy Power does)
- Learned rules now persist into the site profile: upload the registry once and classification, roles, affinities, and self-grades keep applying in every later session without re-uploading it
- The drag-to-teach dialog is now a reviewable checklist: select or deselect any matched sibling, and search to add tags the matcher missed (each shown with the parent it would get)
- Fixed the build completing but never opening results when no electrical sources were selected

- Drag-to-teach: after nesting one tag, the app offers to nest every sibling of the same kind (learned classification or description pattern), each matched to its own parent instance by shared tag numbers
- The generalization shows exactly what it will do (tag → parent list) before applying, applies as a single undo step, and skips anything ambiguous, already placed by hand, or already correct

- Added undo/redo for hierarchy massaging: toolbar buttons plus Cmd/Ctrl+Z and Shift+Cmd/Ctrl+Z, restoring prior overrides exactly (including walking back to derived placement)
- Manually placed rows now carry a pin badge so hand-made moves are visible at a glance
- Spring-loaded folders: hovering a collapsed branch mid-drag opens it
- Fixed a rebuild feedback loop where the resolved register re-ingested its own output as evidence, preventing undo from restoring derived placements
- 1.0: the full loop is complete — documents in, hierarchy compiled with evidence and self-graded inference, weak spots proposed, drag-and-drop massaging with undo, and every correction saved as durable profile knowledge

- Added drag-and-drop hierarchy massaging in the SSM view: drag an equipment row onto another to reparent it, or onto its system folder to make it a root
- Moves persist as relationship overrides in the active profile (session-only on locked profiles), outrank every claim including inferred nesting, and survive rebuilds
- Cross-system-block drops are refused with guidance (those belong in Dependencies), and cycle-creating moves are blocked
- The moved row is revealed and focused after the tree rebuilds

- Nesting inference now BUILDS the hierarchy for self-graded claim classes: the model replays its policy against the registry's own Closest Parent answers per class, and only classes proving >=85% precision nest automatically (evidence always outranks; provenance says inferred)
- Everything below the bar stays a reviewable proposal; benchmarked end-to-end against a real registry at 87% claim precision with 100% root agreement
- Containment rule hardened: extensions must be substantive and continue at a separator boundary (racks and power supplies nest; A/B siblings and short header tags do not)
- Electrical Flow view now lists what an instrument controls beneath it as a marked reference node
- A MEL alone now builds the full register — no electrical sources required

- Added nesting proposals learned from a registry export: Equipment Description decides the role (parent-capable equipment vs child device), number nomenclature picks the instance
- Two rules: deterministic tag-containment (racks, power supplies extend their parent's tag) and role + shared-number + class-pair affinity
- Proposals fill blank Proposed System Parent cells in the Completed MEL with the rationale in Provenance, and land in the QA review queue with runners-up — never silent structural claims
- Inert without a registry to learn from; proposals respect discipline boundaries (candidates come from the same building/discipline/system block)

- Suffix identity unification is now default wiring: when Easy Power, the cable schedule, or PMD spell a tag without the building prefix the MEL carries, an unambiguous back-of-tag match unifies them into one record and the MEL spelling wins
- Claims recorded under any absorbed spelling follow the unified record; ambiguous matches stay separate and surface in review instead of being guessed
- Unification only engages when MEL data is loaded, keeping large no-MEL imports inside the performance budget

- Fixed the corrupted header brand block: the v0.1.0 rebrand had re-injected the old SSManagement title four times inside the tagline, overlapping the page at desktop widths
- Added a build-time regression guard pinning the brand block to exactly one title and one tagline

- Added equipment classification learned from registry descriptions (digit-masked, 0.9 confidence gate; validated ~94% on an 18k-row registry)
- Classification feeds the item-master (discipline, classification, UPN) rung and the Rev21 Equipment Classification column (AJ)
- Provenance records each learned classification with its confidence
